items.problem: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}4&7\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Give the matrix as [a,b;c,d].
items.solution_sketch: Determinant: $8 - 7 = 1$. Swap $4$ and $2$, change the sign of $7$ and $1$. The inverse is [2,-7;-1,4]; check: row 1 times column 1 is $8 - 7 = 1$.

items.problem: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}2&3\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$. Give the matrix as [a,b;c,d].
items.solution_sketch: Determinant: $2 - 3 = -1$. Swapped matrix with changed signs: $\begin{pmatrix}1&-3\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Divide each entry by $-1$: [-1,3;1,-2].

items.problem: Find $A^{-1}$ for $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$. Give the matrix as [a,b;c,d] with fractions.
items.solution_sketch: Determinant: $4 - 6 = -2$. Swapped matrix with changed signs: $\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}$. Divide each entry by $-2$: [-2,1;3/2,-1/2].

items.problem: The inverse of a matrix $A$ is $A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}2&-5\\-1&3\end{pmatrix}$. Find $A$. Give the matrix as [a,b;c,d].
items.solution_sketch: $A$ is the inverse of $A^{-1}$. Determinant of $A^{-1}$: $6 - 5 = 1$. Swap $2$ and $3$, change the sign of $-5$ and $-1$: [3,5;1,2].
